name: PA-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Summer Lee is an incumbent in a district that leans about ten points Democratic
Overwhelming financial edge: about $1.7 million on hand versus roughly $2,500 for James Hayes
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; no competitive signals anywhere in the race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an incumbent in a D+10 district with a cash advantage of several hundred to one, no outside opposition spending, and markets pricing the race as effectively decided. Nothing justifies moving the expected margin materially below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Lee or a surprise poll showing a single-digit margin would be the first sign the race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Summer Lee, a Democratic incumbent, defends a Pittsburgh-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. She was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with roughly $1.7 million on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised about $65,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars in cash. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets price her chances near 97 percent.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. The combination points to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty being how a low-spending challenger and turnout variation might shift the margin rather than the outcome.
